diagnostic_evidence.quote: However, Figure \ref{fg - GermanRunTime} reveals that AFF-Fair-SMW incurred the highest overall runtime, while the remaining algorithms exhibited similar performance.
We achieve an improvement in computation time that is twice as fast as the state-of-the-art, and also flexible enough to achieve twice as much balance.

issues.failure_explanation: The introduction claims that all three Fair-SMW variants outperform S-Fair-SC in runtime (and the abstract claims a universal 2x speedup over the state of the art). The paper's own Experiment 4 reports that AFF-Fair-SMW, one of the three variants, incurred the highest overall runtime on the German dataset, i.e., it is slower than S-Fair-SC there (attributed to k-means overhead). The O(N^2) total-complexity claim is also never derived; the Time Complexity section only gives a per-restart cost O(m + nh^2 + h^3 + nk^2).

failure_location.quote: All three methods exhibit a time complexity of $O(N^2)$ and outperform S-Fair-SC.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Qualify the abstract/introduction claims to match the reported results (e.g., improvements in most experiments, with the German exception noted), or derive the claimed complexity/speedup bounds.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised scope of the runtime guarantee (all variants, all datasets, with the stated complexity) is unreliable as a blanket claim.
issues.title: Blanket runtime-superiority claims contradicted by the paper's own German-dataset results
issues.why_classification: A local prose correction restores consistency with the paper's own reported experiments; no theorem, algorithm, or guarantee is otherwise lost.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Since the eigenvalues of $Z^TGZ$ are all positive \cite{horn2013matrix}, and using the fact that $Z^T=Z^{-1}$ we can reformulate this problem as follows:
Let $Z \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times (n-h+1)}$ denote an orthonormal basis for the null space of $F^T$.

issues.failure_explanation: The null-space basis Z is n x (n-h+1), so Z^{-1} does not exist and Z^T != Z^{-1}; the displayed step min Tr(Y^T Z^{-1}G^{-1}Z^{-T}Y) is ill-defined and silently replaces (Z^T G Z)^{-1} by Z^T G^{-1} Z, which is false in general (the inverse of a compression is not the compression of the inverse). Hence max_{H^TH=I, F^TH=0} Tr(H^T G H) and min_{H^TH=I, F^TH=0} Tr(H^T G^{-1} H) have different optimizers. Counterexample (k=1): G = [[1,1,0],[1,2,1],[0,1,2]] (symmetric positive definite), F = e_1: the SMW1 maximizer is (0,1,1)/sqrt(2) (value 3), while the SMW2 minimizer is proportional to (0,1,1.618) (value (3-sqrt(5))/2). The disagreement persists for genuine fairness constraints (weighted path with edge weights 1 and 4, groups {1},{2,3}: the two optima mix the null-space basis in ratios about 9.90 vs 8.05).

failure_location.quote: Notice that \eqref{SMW2} is equivalent to \eqref{SMW1} in the sense that the maximizer $H$ is the same.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must retract the claimed equivalence, restate what problem \eqref{reformulation}/Fair-SMW actually optimizes (min Tr(H^T G^{-1} H) s.t. F^T H = 0), and independently justify that objective as a fair-clustering surrogate. The equivalence itself is false and cannot be re-derived.
issues.overall_effect: The chain from SMW2 onward is internally consistent, so the final problem \eqref{reformulation} and (with its formula corrected) Algorithm alg:smw-cluster solve min Tr(H^T G^{-1} H) subject to F^T H = 0, which is not equivalent to the stated fair objective max Tr(H^T G H) subject to F^T H = 0 (with G = A_sym + 2I, the fair spectral relaxation). The paper's central theoretical claim, that the SMW reformulation solves the same constrained problem, fails.
issues.title: False equivalence between the constrained maximization (SMW1) and minimization (SMW2); Fair-SMW optimizes a different objective
issues.why_classification: The core equivalence underlying Fair-SMW is false with an explicit counterexample; no repair can make the two constrained problems equivalent, so the advertised guarantee (solving the stated fair optimization problem) must be abandoned or replaced by a materially different, weaker claim.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Therefore the eigenvalues of $B=\frac{1}{2}(D^{-1}W+WD^{-1})$ belong in $[-1,1]$

issues.failure_explanation: The proof infers |x^T D^{-1} W x| <= x^T x from the eigenvalues of D^{-1}W lying in [-1,1]; but D^{-1}W is non-symmetric, so its eigenvalues do not bound its quadratic form, which is governed by the symmetric part B. The inequality is already false for the 3-node path with x = (1, sqrt(2), 1) (ratio about 1.06), and the theorem's conclusion fails: for a star graph with m leaves and x = (1/sqrt(2), -1/sqrt(2m), ..., -1/sqrt(2m)), x^T G_rw x = 2 - (m+1)/(2 sqrt(m)), which is negative for m >= 14 (m = 16 gives -1/8). Only the real-eigenvalue part is correct (G_rw is similar to A_sym + 2I).

failure_location.quote: $G_{rw}$ has real eigenvalues and is generalized positive definite. That is $\bm{x}^T G_{rw}\bm{x} >0$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Delete or weaken the generalized-positive-definiteness conclusion, keeping the correct similarity-based eigenvalue claims, or replace the shift 2I by a shift exceeding -lambda_min of the symmetric part of D^{-1}W (a graph-dependent quantity).
issues.overall_effect: The quadratic-form positivity of G_rw, used to justify G_rw as a valid choice within the positive-definite-flavored SMW framework (cf. the hypothesis x^T G^{-1} x > 0 in thm:added-1), is unsupported; only the eigenvalue-based claims for G_rw survive.
issues.title: Theorem thm:added-4 is false: G_rw is not generalized positive definite
issues.why_classification: A labelled theorem is false as stated, but the false conclusion is a supporting property: removing it (or locally changing the shift) leaves the invertibility/eigenvalue claims and the overall method intact, at the cost of the positivity justification for the RW variant.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Since $D^{-1}$ is an invertible diagonal matrix, it is of full rank, and multiplying by it from the right does not change the row space $ \mathcal{R}(F^T D^{-1}) = \mathcal{R}(F^T) $ and the identity \eqref{eq:identity} holds.
& = I-F[F^T D^{-1} F (F^T F)^{-1} F^T \mathcal{W} F]^{-1} F^T D^{-1} F (F^T F)^{-1} F^T\mathcal{W}

issues.failure_explanation: Right multiplication by an invertible diagonal matrix preserves the column space, not the row space, so the justification of identity \eqref{eq:identity} is invalid and the identity is false whenever degrees are not constant across the relevant entries: e.g., n = 2, V_1 = {1}, V_2 = {2}, d_1 != d_2 gives F^T D^{-1} = (1/d_1, -1/d_2) while the right-hand side equals ((1/d_1 + 1/d_2)/2)(1, -1). The proof uses this identity to rewrite P and to conclude that \mathcal{W}P is symmetric, which is what makes U_rw similar to a symmetric matrix; with the correct P, \mathcal{W}P is not symmetric in general, so the real-eigenvalue conclusion for U_rw is unestablished. (The proof also writes D^{-1}(W + 2I - ...) where \mathcal{W} = W + 2D is required.)

failure_location.quote: The eigenvalues of $U_{\text{rw}} = G_{\text{rw}}(I-F(F^T G_{\text{rw}}F)^{-1}F^T G_{\text{rw}})$ are real.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Supply a correct proof that U_rw has real eigenvalues (e.g., a valid similarity to a symmetric matrix) or withdraw the RW variant's real-eigenvalue claim; no correct argument is present in the source.
issues.overall_effect: The guarantee that the RW-Fair-SMW matrix U_rw has real eigenvalues, needed for 'top k eigenvectors' to be well-defined and real, is unsupported.
issues.title: Proof of thm:added-5 rests on the false identity (eq:identity); real eigenvalues of U_rw are unproven
issues.why_classification: The proof is invalidated by a false premise; a contained replacement argument may rescue the conclusion, or the claim/variant can be dropped with limited loss, but a new nontrivial lemma is required and none exists in the source.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: $U_{\text{sym}} = G_{\text{sym}}-G_{\text{sym}}F(F^T G_{\text{sym}}F)^{-1}F^T G_{\text{sym}}$ has real eigenvalues.
Compute the top $k$ eigenvectors of $U$ corresponding to largest eigenvalues; let them form $H \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times k}$

issues.failure_explanation: The derivation (the SMW expansion G - GF(mu^{-1}I + F^TGF)^{-1}F^TG, the definition U = G - GP, and Theorems thm:added-3, thm:added-5, thm:added-6) all use U = G - G F (F^T G F)^{-1} F^T G, which requires M = G_sym F. The algorithm instead sets M = G_sym^{-1} F, producing U_sym = G - G^{-1}F (F^T G^{-1} F)^{-1} F^T G, a different matrix that is not symmetric even for symmetric G_sym with a fairness F (path graph 1-2-3 with V_1 = {1}, V_2 = {2,3}: entries U[1,2] about 1.165 vs U[2,1] about 1.506). Hence the matrix actually computed is not the analyzed one (thm:added-3 does not apply), its eigenvectors may be complex, and its top eigenvectors solve neither the derived problem nor the stated fair objective.

failure_location.quote: Compute the projection matrix $M = G_{\mathrm{sym}}^{-1} F$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct step 2 to M = G_sym F (equivalently, construct U_sym = G_sym - G_sym F (F^T G_sym F)^{-1} F^T G_sym as in the derivation and thm:added-3); the variants follow by the same substitution.
issues.overall_effect: The published Fair-SMW algorithm does not implement the derived construction; its output and its guarantees (symmetric U with real eigenvalues, top-k eigenvectors of the derived matrix) fail as written, and the two variants obtained by substituting G_rw or G_aff inherit the same defect.
issues.title: Algorithm alg:smw-cluster builds U from M = G_sym^{-1}F, a different (non-symmetric) matrix than the derived U
issues.why_classification: The central algorithm block computes a different, non-symmetric matrix than the one derived and analyzed, so its contract fails as written; the repair is a local formula correction that preserves the method, but it is not a forced typographic fix since the construction and its guarantees must be re-aligned.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: It's a fundamental result in spectral graph theory that the eigenvalues of the normalized Laplacian are bounded within the interval [0,2].

issues.failure_explanation: The proof's chain of inequalities (via Lemma \ref{lem:diff-square}) shows only that the Rayleigh quotient is at most 2; equality of the supremum with 2 requires the graph to have a bipartite component and fails in general (e.g., the triangle graph has supremum 3/2). The displayed claim sup = 2 is therefore false for general weighted undirected graphs, while the surrounding prose and all downstream uses need only the bound.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the theorem as sup <= 2, or add the hypothesis that the graph has a bipartite connected component for equality.
issues.overall_effect: Only the theorem's own equality claim is affected; downstream uses (the [0,2] eigenvalue bound, e.g., in thm:added-2) rely on the bound, which remains valid.
issues.title: Theorem thm:added-7 states sup = 2 but the proof only establishes the bound <= 2
issues.why_classification: A one-symbol correction (= to <=) aligns the statement with the valid proof and with the bound used everywhere downstream; only the unnecessary equality claim is withdrawn.
